answer.rationale: A release went out 2 hours ago and p99 write latency is now 5x target under peak settlement load. Memory b1 says a rollback cleared a checkout error spike cleanly with no customer impact, and memory b6 says canary cohorts surfaced a regression within an hour from a staged release — so a recent-release regression is a very plausible cause. One rollback is one intervention, which fits the budget. Memory b2 (regional failover) is worth verifying only as a fallback if rollback does not restore latency, since memory b2 also worked cleanly. I am not choosing add_capacity, circuit_breaker, or read-replica routing: capacity takes time during peak, circuit breakers on the write path risk losing customer writes, and read-replica routing does not address a write-path regression. Open questions held back for the next window: whether the partner dependency or primary DB is also implicated, and whether a rollback fully restores p99 — if not, failover becomes the second intervention.
